truth.claim: Literary Digest 1936: 10,000,000 mailed, 2,376,523 returned, Landon 57 % / Roosevelt 43 %, Gallup 50,000 -> 56 %, result 61 %, 18 points off, 48x
18 of 30: plausible 42 % to 78 %; Wilson lower also 42 %
truth.note: Wald 60 ± 17.5; Wilson lower 42.3 %; the honest limits note the exact (Clopper-Pearson) lower is 40.6 %

truth.claim: a 50 % market gives 18+ of 30 in 18 % of surveys; seeded 20 surveys range 10 to 20 of 30, 4 at 18+; 1,000-surveys within 3 points (474 to 527)
truth.note: all 42 formulas recompute; binomial tail P(X >= 18 | 30, 0.5) = 0.181

defects.what: The closing frame carries seven text items (18 of 30, AS LOW AS 42 %, YOU 55 %, PLAUSIBLE 42 % TO 78 %, BELOW HALF IS INSIDE, the ± ledger, the dot strip) around one short rail; the answer (42 %) is not the largest thing on it
'60 %' is the first big number on screen (hook, 4 to 8 s); the 18-of-30 dots precede it, so the letter of counts-first holds, but the film opens on a percentage and the commit is asked in percent
The Digest/Gallup/result rail stacks four labels (DIGEST 43, LANDON 57, GALLUP 56, RESULT 61) in two sizes over three ticks within 20 units; readable at 1080, cramped

one_line: Twenty surveys of thirty from a market you know is 50/50 is the right count, and the Digest case is told straight; the last frame tries to say five things at once.
